title: CGI and D-Wave Partner to Commercialize Enterprise Quantum Optimization Across Transportation, Logistics, and Retail - Quantum Computing Report
gist: CGI (NYSE: GIB) and D-Wave (NASDAQ: QBTS) signed a strategic go-to-market partnership, after over a year of technical work, in which CGI will integrate D-Wave's Advantage2 annealing QPU and hybrid solvers into its IT services portfolio. The joint work targets optimization in rail, retail/supply chain, and industrial/energy operations, with engagement models to move clients from proof-of-concept to production.

insights.claim: CGI Inc. (NYSE: GIB, TSX: GIB.A) and D-Wave Quantum (NASDAQ: QBTS) formed a strategic go-to-market partnership under which CGI will integrate D-Wave's Advantage2 annealing QPU cloud access and hybrid solver services into its global IT services portfolio, building on over a year of technical collaboration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A large systems integrator acting as a reseller channel could widen D-Wave's enterprise distribution; watch for disclosed CGI-sourced bookings in QBTS results.
insights.locator: Global IT consulting firm CGI Inc.

insights.claim: The partnership pairs D-Wave's quantum annealing hardware with CGI's systems integration footprint of 94,000 consultants across enterprise logistics, transportation, and public sector domains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Distribution through integrators, not direct sales, is how a small quantum vendor can reach enterprise buyers at scale.
insights.locator: The joint initiative pairs CGI's global systems integration footprint

insights.claim: CGI CTO Dave Henderson and D-Wave Chief Revenue Officer Lorenzo Martinelli lead a collaboration offering structured engagement models to move clients from proof-of-concept validation to full production deployment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: D-Wave's CRO leading the deal signals a revenue-focused push; the key watch item is conversion of pilots into recurring production contracts.

insights.claim: CGI and D-Wave target transportation and rail (train scheduling and dispatching, yard traffic, rolling stock and crew allocation), retail and supply chain (multi-echelon inventory, last-mile routing, workforce scheduling), and industrial/energy (production throughput, grid load balancing, maintenance scheduling) using Advantage2, Leap cloud, and constrained quadratic model solvers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Combinatorial scheduling and routing are the near-term commercial wedge for annealing-based quantum; logistics and rail operators are the likely early customers.
insights.locator: CGI & D-Wave Joint Enterprise Solution Portfolio

insights.claim: The CGI–D-Wave applications are positioned to augment rather than replace classical computing, with enterprises adopting hybrid quantum-classical solvers for real-time operational workflows that the article says exceed legacy classical systems' capabilities.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid augmentation is the adoption narrative; the claim of exceeding classical capabilities is unquantified in the release and warrants skepticism.
